venues.name: CC Nashville
venues.narrative: **CCNSH — Sunday 8/16** (MOD & Chef: KE, DM) A good Sunday night with very fun vibes throughout. Fairly slow up until 7pm; the bulk of sales landed between 7-9pm. After 9pm the room stayed steady with a consistent flow of guests until close, with lots of regulars in as usual. Two promising new guests, Pat and Colleen — both musicians — are likely to become regulars; they took a late, entertainingly loud group in stride and laughed it off, making for a great outro to the evening. Comps of $66.70 (4.1%) were mostly a gift to guests new to the neighborhood. Kitchen: Danny is locking into his role. 86 High Life. No incidents. Net sales $1,623 against a $1,441 target (+12.6%), 63 guests, $25.76 check average, food $195. Entered by BT. Note: the Typeform day-of-week field was mis-keyed as Saturday; post time and narrative confirm this is the Sunday 8/16 report.

venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.narrative: **DVR — Sunday 8/16** (AM MOD: Maggie H; PM MOD & Chef: Maggie H & Rachel) Scattered showers at the start of the night seemed to keep most people home — slow and steady in The Garden and The Lobby. Segment splits: DC/AM $867.73, D&C (PM) $9,282.94, Garden/6A $1,694.35; total net sales $10,150.67 against a $10,303 target (-1.5%), 299 guests (Tock), $33.95 check average, food $2,217.30, comps $384.70. No events. AM: Kodi's first DC/AM report — slower day with no IRDs and mostly espresso martinis; batched a liter of Conference and upsold it successfully, swapped the steaming pitcher rack and right coffee urn for efficiency, and deep-cleaned the espresso cleaning-equipment bin. 86 Saratoga Sparkling; low on 16oz iced cups and kombucha. PM: Ryan and Kyle caught a nice pop right at open; Kim and Minsu pushed through drink tickets with ease. Steady 5-7pm, then a gradual trickle down. Lots of exhausted staff — reminder to hydrate and prioritize sleep. Soda Club's first soft-open Friends & Family night is Monday 8/17 next door. Garden/6A: last leg of the Nana Daq in Mr. Frosty; one of the prettiest Garden nights in days, but RiNo was sleepy. Kitchen: slow night, got the grease trays under the grill and ranges cleaned; decent prep tomorrow. Maintenance: reminder that building issues go to the hotel front desk for Intelity first, then the maintenance channel. Entered by mjh.

venues.name: D&C East Village
venues.narrative: **EV — Sunday 8/16** (MOD: Thomas; no chef) Rain throughout the night. A pretty slow first turn that heated up for two hours but never hit a legit flow — expected quiet for the end of the weekend after the preceding busier days. Net sales $3,761 against a $3,533 target (+6.5%), 110 covers, $34 check average, food $132, beverage $3,589, retail $40, comps $114.56. Zero large parties, 4 solos, 2 investor cocktails. Top sellers: Rosalie, Burner Phone, Native Lion, Eight Limb Daiquiri. Service note: it pays to talk to guests — won over a Kansas City couple with Tech N9ne and Clipse knowledge. Door (KN): a wonderful drizzly evening with relatively light foot traffic, but the room stayed pretty full for most of the night. Had to turn away a couple of reservations for lack of IDs on '21-year-old' guests. Lots of midwestern visitors. Emptied out around 11:30pm and closed with a few industry folks at the bar. No-shows: Mark Sumner (1, 7:30pm), Christian Moro (2, 8pm), Joseph Bennett (4, 11pm) — not charged. No glassware breakage. Maintenance: kitchen sink is not draining. Entered by Thomas.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.narrative: **LA — Sunday 8/16** (MOD & Chef: Joe + Josh + Oscar) A busy Sunday evening. Started with 40 covers on the books and a strong open — the bar top filled quickly with the rest of the room following soon after. Lots going on in the Arts District that afternoon had people bar hopping. A couple of guests arrived too intoxicated and were kindly asked to come back another night; they left without hesitation. Steady walk-ins kept the room nearly full most of the night, clearing out slowly over the last couple of hours with lots of familiar faces. Jazz crushed it on the floor, keeping every table in good hands. Smooth close with good vibes. Net sales $5,128 against a $4,806 target (+6.7%), 132 guests, $38.85 check average, food $1,054, comps $51.48 (Howlin' Rays crew, Dinora + Martin, birthday, DNL). No standing room sales. Kitchen steady. Maintenance: oven isn't heating up, ResQ order placed. 86 cookies and tuna. No-shows charged. Favorite moment: Jorge making quesadillas at end of night. Entered by Joe.

venues.name: D&C Washington DC
venues.narrative: **DC — Sunday 8/16** (MOD: Josh) Slow start with the weather working against us, including some light rain; Garden closed. The team stayed productive through the slower stretches with sidework, cleaning and resetting glassware. Around 7pm things picked up with a good run of two-top walk-ins that carried a nice push through the rest of the evening. Service ran smoothly and guests really enjoyed the National Rum Day offerings — a nice finish to the night. Marquee bar sales $2,365.30, food $136, total net sales including events $2,257.30 against a $2,758 target (-18.2%), 53 guests, $41.04 guest check average, comps $108 (rang wrong item). Went well: ABK, menu insert. To improve: label and date. Maintenance: KD ice machine missing a bolt; point rail. No incidents. Entered by Josh. Note: the Typeform date field was mis-keyed as 2026-08-14; day-of-week (Sunday) and post time confirm this is the 8/16 report.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.narrative: **MG — Sunday 8/16** (AM MOD & Chef: Sam & Lex; PM MOD & Chef: Justin & Shannon) Total net sales $10,019 against a $6,000 target (+67.0%), 207 guests (117 morning / 90 evening), $48.40 check average, food $3,235, event sales $1,959, comps $985 (believed to include an event discount). Outlet splits: Municipal Bar morning $3,135, Municipal Bar evening $3,676, Sun Club $130, Hot Eye $1,078. Morning: slower start with few IRD orders, but picked up from 11am and by noon had 13 tables seated plus bar guests. Team helped each other well; only two larger parties. Ticket times fell behind from 11:30 for about an hour. James rocked the bar. Evening: a generally chill night, slightly short-staffed but the slow pace caused no long waits. Guests from the mezzanine event came downstairs for drinks, keeping Chandler and Amelia busy without being overwhelming. A few late campers; all guests out by 11:30. Closed with one bartender, one barback, one server and one SA — as effective as a typical close. The alarm reportedly went off (no one on the team heard it) and authorities found no cause. Sun Club: groups early before a solid 2pm storm knocked down a tree and three umbrellas — all reset; told a guest smoking he wasn't allowed and he complied; the Sun Club elevator still isn't responding to the call button. Hot Eye: fun solo night, mellow early with hotel guests and industry, the usual bar crawl came through around 9 (bigger than normal) with Justin's help, then a heavy local service-industry presence; sold all 5 burritos. Kitchen: 86'd hash browns for the caviar set, low on cucumbers. Event: chorus event on the Mezzanine 8-10pm, Eva solo bartended for ~50 with stationed food; space was tight but the group was easy to host, and Hot Eye glassware was used again. Event revenue again posted to the Sun Club revenue center in error, and the final bill is $50 off on taxes after the event discount, though all net sales were captured. Maintenance: left elevator not responding from the roof; Franck to have Impact Fire address the alarm; Hot Eye floors and men's room need attention. Entered by Sam B.
